d2f4168868c9c9bf5764bc3a92c6399e4b6d5d1d.summary: Threat report titled 'Iron Tiger Compromises Chat Application Mimi, Targets Windows, Mac, and Linux Users'. The page is mainly an indicator-of-compromise list: SHA256 hashes for HyperBro DLL and packed payload samples (Windows) and Rshell samples (Linux and Mac OS), plus network addresses, command-and-control endpoints and download locations. The text gives no narrative on attribution, sectors, countries, CVEs or dates of activity, and it states no caveats of its own. The only dated item is the page archive date.

d26705e3fbce5f32c31647f3388f8eb19b4472df.summary: This page is a reference index for the BONDUPDATER malware family, published by Fraunhofer FKIE and archived on 2026-04-05. It lists the family's alias names (Poison Frog, Glimpse) and links it to the actors OilRig and APT34. Its reference list gives titles, dates and authors of public reports from 2018 to 2020 by various vendors and researchers. The page has no description of its own and no YARA signature. It is an index, not a threat report, so it contributes no facts.
hedges: There is no description at this point.

d21d80f8069cbea69621a907c594ab572b487c04.summary: Deep Instinct researchers describe Arid Gopher, a Go-written malware variant that they link to the Arid Viper group, based on code and functionality similarities. Arid Gopher is a Go version of Micropsia, emailed to targets in archive files, with a backdoor and a decoy document. Arid Viper is described as an APT group believed to be based in Gaza, with use focused on Palestinian targets in the Middle East.
